question: Does a published-geometry moving-object pulse elicit DNa02 firing in the selected MaleCNS route?
status: offline sensitivity study; no playable change or biological calibration

protocol.fly: Fixed at origin; no movement or motor feedback.
protocol.source_pulse_geometry: 22.5-degree azimuth sweeps at 25 or 75 degrees/s follow Collie et al.; centers at 25 and 45 degrees are our model probes.
protocol.input: Upstream-derived LC10a rank map; full 90 mV current normalized across the stimulated side. Position or previous magnitude-only motion factor. All per-cell retinal angles and current amplitudes are unmeasured assumptions.
protocol.sensitivity: AOTU-to-DNa02 model edge currents scaled by 1, 2, or 4; symmetric tonic DNa02 current-equivalent drive at 0, 16, or 20 mV. The latter straddle this LIF model's 15 mV steady-state firing threshold. None is a measured parameter.
protocol.control: All four AOTU-to-DNa02 edges removed with otherwise identical stimulus, tonic drive, cells, and LIF state.
protocol.interpretation: A positive toward-side spike difference must also exceed the bridge-removed control; static and reversed sweeps test selectivity. This is a sensitivity analysis, not fitted physiology.
